evidence_atlas.label: tab:frontier-atlas
evidence_atlas.caption: Representative frontier evidence atlas. P and S denote primary and secondary fields. Citations identify the works; locators specify the source version where needed. Source labels describe the consulted documents rather than later publication status. Each claim should be read together with its locator and limit; evidence level is not a ranking of model quality.

rows.name: OpenVLA
rows.claim: OpenVLA provides an open 7B VLA baseline trained on the Open X-Embodiment mixture and reports higher author-run success than RT-2-X.
rows.locator: arXiv v3, Tables 4–6; Appendix D.1, Table 9.
rows.limit: Action-policy evidence; no explicit dynamics or consequence model.

rows.name: RoboDreamer
rows.claim: RoboDreamer generates compositional video plans for unseen instructions and periodically replans during RLBench execution.
rows.locator: arXiv v1, Secs. 2.2, 4.1–4.2; Table 3.
rows.limit: Robot execution is evaluated in simulation; real-robot datasets support video-generation evaluation, not physical closed-loop deployment.

rows.name: DexMimicGen
rows.claim: DexMimicGen extends object-centric demonstration transformation to bimanual and dexterous manipulation.
rows.locator: arXiv v2, Sec. IV; Sec. VI-D; Fig. 6.
rows.limit: Assumes observable reference-object poses before contact and may inherit simulator or source-strategy bias.

rows.name: Robotic World Model
rows.claim: RWM combines dual-autoregressive dynamics learning with MBPO-PPO and deploys the resulting policies zero-shot on ANYmal D and Unitree G1.
rows.locator: arXiv v5, Sec. 4.4; Fig. 5; Table 1; hardware results in Fig. 1.
rows.limit: Velocity-tracking evidence; not a general manipulation result.

rows.name: WorldPlanner
rows.claim: WorldPlanner combines an action-conditioned visual model, diffusion action sampler, reward model, and MCTS planning followed by MPC tracking.
rows.locator: arXiv v1, Secs. III-E–III-F, IV-F; Fig. 1.
rows.limit: Bounded by the play-data distribution, tested horizons, latency, and possible model exploitation.

rows.name: WorldEval
rows.claim: WorldEval conditions video generation on Policy2Vec embeddings and compares generated-video policy rankings with paired real outcomes.
rows.limit: Paired ranking evidence; no demonstrated gain from using the evaluator to select or update a deployed policy.

rows.name: Towards Safe Robot Foundation Models
rows.claim: An ATACOM-based post-policy layer constrains generalist-policy actions and prevents collisions in an air-hockey evaluation.
rows.locator: Secs. II–III; Figs. 1–2.
rows.limit: Physical air-hockey evidence under specified dynamics and constraints; no learned world-model contribution is isolated.

rows.name: World-in-World
rows.claim: World-in-World evaluates generative models through four closed-loop embodied tasks and separates decision utility from visual quality.
rows.locator: Fig. 1; main tables; controllability, post-training, and inference-compute ablations.
rows.limit: Closed-loop benchmark environments rather than real-robot deployment.

rows.name: Interactive World Simulator
rows.mechanism: Supervised prediction; downstream data generation / evaluation
rows.claim: Interactive World Simulator reports stable interaction beyond 10 minutes at 15 FPS and relates generated-data and simulated-ranking results to real policies.
rows.locator: arXiv v1, Secs. IV-B–IV-D; Figs. 4–7.
rows.limit: Author-run tasks and hardware; correlation may not transfer to novel sensors, policies, or contacts.

rows.name: SimFoundry
rows.claim: Reconstructed twins and generated cousins support policy training and evaluation. Simulated versus physical success yields mean Pearson r=0.911 and MMRV =0.018 across seven tasks and five policy types.
rows.locator: arXiv v4, Secs. 4, 5.1–5.2; Appendix B (FAQ); Table G.1.
rows.limit: Experiments include minutes of manual scene tuning; agreement covers the evaluated task–policy pairs, without establishing absolute calibration.

rows.name: PointWorld
rows.claim: PointWorld predicts full-scene 3D point flow and uses MPPI to optimize Franka trajectories without task-specific demonstrations or post-training.
rows.locator: arXiv v1, Secs. 3.2, 5.4; Appendix A.6.1–A.6.3.
rows.limit: Eight tasks, ten initial configurations each; manually specified spatial goals. Experiments do not replan online; model inference time excludes the full planning cost.

rows.name: TrAct
rows.claim: Track-conditioned candidate selection reaches 76% success on Franka, versus 66% for action-conditioned selection with the same action–track proposal policy.
rows.locator: arXiv v3, Secs. 3.3, 5.4; Table 4; Appendix A, Algorithm 1.
rows.limit: Five tasks under two backgrounds, with ten trials per condition; author-run hardware evaluation.

rows.name: Hydra-0
rows.claim: Action-flow conditioning preserves recorded-trajectory outcomes in RoboLab video replay; desired object flow also conditions inverse motion prediction.
rows.limit: Quantitative evaluation fixes recorded motion before generation; real inverse execution is a qualitative example.

rows.name: Masked Visual Actions
rows.claim: Masked visual actions support RoboCasa candidate selection and inverse action extraction; physical-data tests compare predicted progress with recorded demonstrations.
rows.limit: Planning and inverse-policy tests use RoboCasa; physical evidence replays recorded demonstrations and retains optimistic progress bias.

rows.name: Cosmos 3
rows.claim: Cosmos 3 describes one mixture-of-transformers family for language, image, video, audio, and action input–output configurations.
rows.locator: Technical-report abstract; architecture figure; modality and WAM evaluation sections.
rows.limit: Broad technical-report evidence; robot claims remain model- and task-specific.

rows.name: V-JEPA 2
rows.claim: V-JEPA 2 post-trains an action-conditioned latent model on under 62 hours of DROID video and deploys image-goal planning in two labs.
rows.locator: Fig. 1; V-JEPA 2-AC section; two-lab result tables.
rows.limit: Franka image-goal evaluation; not general action prediction or arbitrary embodiment transfer.

rows.name: DreamGen
rows.claim: DreamGen generates video trajectories and recovers pseudo-actions, reporting 22 new humanoid behaviors from one teleoperated task.
rows.locator: arXiv v1, Secs. 2–4; behavior-generalization results in Sec. 3.2.
rows.limit: Selected GR1 tasks and environments; video fidelity alone is not the downstream claim.

rows.name: DreamZero
rows.claim: DreamZero jointly predicts video and actions with a 14B WAM, reporting more than 2× generalization gains and 7 Hz closed-loop execution.
rows.locator: Abstract; unseen-task and environment tables; latency table; cross-embodiment experiments.
rows.limit: Author-reported robots, tasks, baselines, and data budgets; not universal zero-shot control.

rows.name: Flex-π
rows.claim: Each task's fine-tuned checkpoint supports action-only or full-joint generation on bimanual YAM, refreshing observations between action chunks. Joint generation improves the reported average partial-credit completion score at additional compute cost.
rows.locator: arXiv v3, Secs. 3.2, 4.2, 4.5; Appendices C, F.2, G.1.
rows.limit: Five tasks; 20 trials per task except Sort Utensils (10). Results depend on inference mode and task protocol; baseline task coverage differs.

rows.name: EgoWAM
rows.claim: EgoWAM compares pixel, DINO, and 3D-motion-flow prediction targets under a matched human–robot co-training pipeline.
rows.locator: Secs. 3.2, 4.3; Fig. 1; matched target and bimanual task comparisons.
rows.limit: Three-task study; the world head supplies training supervision and is removed at inference.

rows.name: Puffin-World
rows.claim: Predicts camera orientation and jointly generates RGB-D views for 3D reconstruction, with controlled camera and geometry benchmarks.
rows.limit: Camera-view generation and reconstruction; the self-calibration loop adjusts generated views, not a physical robot. No robot-policy or contact-force evaluation.

rows.name: SolarWM
rows.claim: Unifies data preparation and backbone adaptation; its 5B causal student demonstrates a 60-minute camera-conditioned rollout after five-second-sequence training.
rows.locator: Secs. 4–7; Fig. 11.
rows.limit: Long-horizon evidence is qualitative, with prescribed cameras and fixed prompts; no measured robot-policy gains.

rows.name: PERSIST
rows.claim: PERSIST maintains a latent 3D scene state to improve spatial memory and long-horizon consistency over pixel-history baselines.
rows.locator: arXiv v2, Secs. 4, 6.1; Tables 1–2; Appendices B–C.
rows.limit: Generated environments; no downstream robot-policy or contact evidence.

rows.name: VLAW
rows.claim: VLAW alternates real rollouts for model improvement with weighted flow-matching policy updates on successful real and synthetic trajectories.
rows.locator: Sec. 4.2, Eq. (4), Algorithm 1; synthetic-rollout ablation.
rows.limit: The regularized-RL interpretation does not make the implemented update a policy-gradient method; isolate synthetic-data gains.

rows.name: VLA-RFT
rows.claim: VLA-RFT fine-tunes a VLA through action-conditioned learned-simulator rollouts with trajectory rewards computed from predicted states.
rows.limit: Simulation evidence; reward verification here does not establish real-outcome validity or immunity to simulator exploitation.

rows.name: VT-WAM
rows.claim: VT-WAM jointly predicts future vision, tactile deformation, and actions, reporting 71.67% average success across six real tasks.
rows.locator: arXiv v1, Fig. 2; Secs. IV-C–IV-D, Tables I–III.
rows.limit: Author-run hardware and sensors; cross-sensor and cross-object transfer remain bounded.

rows.name: RoboArena
rows.claim: RoboArena aggregates distributed, pairwise double-blind real-robot comparisons over a DROID evaluator network.
rows.locator: Fig. 1; distributed protocol; ranking and reliability tables.
rows.limit: Coverage depends on participating sites, policies, resets, and tasks; the ranking is not universal capability.

glossary.label: tab:glossary
glossary.caption: Glossary of loop terms used in the survey.

rows.name: World model
cells: learned model that predicts action-dependent future consequences (Section 2.2)
not every large model is automatically a world model

rows.name: Prediction-to-Control Gap
cells: the observation that accurate predictions need not improve decisions

rows.name: Consumer
cells: learner, policy, planner, evaluator or monitor that reads the model's output
model quality is relative to the consumer

rows.name: Design dial
cells: one of four questions that specify a world model, each with a trade-off
routes are dial settings, not rival paradigms

rows.name: Prediction space (Y)
cells: what the model predicts, from pixels to task quantities
not the same as the feature pathway

rows.name: Conditioning (C)
cells: what the prediction is conditioned on, from passive video to robot actions or joint generation
instruction conditioning is not action conditioning

rows.name: Knowledge source (D)
cells: where the model's knowledge comes from: web or human video, simulation, robot interaction

rows.name: Computation (M)
cells: how a prediction is computed and how long it takes
a slow model cannot serve a fast consumer

rows.name: Pathway
cells: what the model hands to its consumer; labels a use, not a paper
one system may use several pathways

rows.name: Features pathway
cells: prediction shapes the state a policy acts on
no rollout is needed at decision time

rows.name: Experience pathway
cells: generated trajectories or demonstrations serve as training data
generated data must be judged by downstream transfer

rows.name: Scores pathway
cells: model returns reward, success, progress or cost estimates

rows.name: Decisions pathway
cells: predicted futures of candidate actions select the current action

rows.name: Residuals pathway
cells: difference between prediction and observation corrects behavior without parameter updates
correction is not adaptation of parameters

rows.name: Outer loop
cells: deployment data refit the model or the policy
queries drift as the policy improves

rows.name: Closed-loop utility
cells: improvement in robot behavior caused by using the model in the loop
success, return, sample efficiency, safety, transfer
not the same as open-loop prediction quality

rows.name: Imagination
cells: use of predicted futures for planning, training, or evaluation

rows.name: Neural simulator
cells: learned model used as an environment surrogate for policy training or evaluation

rows.name: Monitor
cells: deployment component that tracks uncertainty, OOD state, contact mismatch, or predicted failure

rows.name: Failure library
cells: structured record of predicted and real failed episodes
failures should be categorized by pathway

rows.name: Query distribution
cells: states and actions on which the model is actually used by a consumer
planner proposals, policy rollouts, deployment shifts
random held-out test data may be insufficient

rows.name: Model exploitation
cells: planner or policy finds behavior that maximizes model score but fails in reality
especially important for decisions and learned rewards

rows.name: Support constraint
cells: offline-RL or safety condition that limits out-of-distribution actions
uncertainty is useful only if it affects decisions

rows.name: Foundation prior
cells: pretrained knowledge that initializes representation, policy, prediction, critic, or simulator
foundation scale does not imply closed-loop evidence

rows.name: VLA policy
cells: vision-language-action model that maps context to robot actions
a consumer of predictions; a world model only if it predicts action-dependent futures

rows.name: World foundation model
cells: large model trained to predict or simulate broad world dynamics
must still be grounded in robot control utility

rows.name: Tactile grounding
cells: use of touch/contact signals to improve prediction, planning, or correction
modality count is not the contribution

rows.name: Closed-loop utility
cells: measured improvement in learned or executed policy

rows.name: Deployment reliability
cells: behavior under real-world shift, failures, and interventions
success rate alone can hide unsafe execution

rows.name: Evidence boundary
cells: explicit statement of what a paper's evidence does not prove
especially needed for technical reports and demos

rows.name: Pathway-removal ablation
cells: experiment disabling or replacing a claimed world-model pathway

rows.name: Action-conditioned metric
cells: metric evaluated under candidate actions relevant to control

rows.name: Generated-data ablation
cells: comparison of real-only, generated-only, and mixed training
prevents synthetic data from being assumed helpful

rows.name: Calibration
cells: agreement between predicted confidence/scores and real outcomes

rows.name: Human correction
cells: intervention, preference, instruction, or repair signal from a person
human input is part of the loop, not only annotation

rows.name: Auditable system
cells: system with inspectable pathways, evidence, failures, and fallback conditions

reporting_checklist.label: tab:min-reporting-checklist
reporting_checklist.caption: Minimum reporting checklist for future robot world-model papers.

rows.name: Pathway
cells: what the model hands over, to which consumer, and when
calling the whole system a world model without specifying the pathway

rows.name: Robot/task scope
cells: embodiments, sensors, action spaces, tasks, horizons
aggregate task counts without physical variables

rows.name: Training data
cells: real/sim/generated mixture, demonstrations, failures, human labels
no breakdown of generated vs. real data effect

rows.name: Optimization signal
cells: imitation loss, reward, value, calibration, uncertainty, intervention
links model learning to policy improvement

rows.name: Query distribution
cells: demonstration, planner proposal, policy rollout, deployment shift

rows.name: Baselines
cells: policy-only, model-free, scripted reward, simulator-only, real-data-only
tests whether the world-model pathway adds value
comparing only to weaker architecture variants

rows.name: Metrics
cells: model quality, closed-loop utility, deployment reliability
prevents prediction quality from replacing utility
reporting success without safety or intervention cost

rows.name: Failure cases
cells: negative examples, uncertainty, recovery, suspected pathway failure
only successful videos or averaged results

rows.name: Artifacts
cells: code, data, benchmark, model, videos, logs, or evidence label
unclear boundary between demos and evaluated trials
